messages:
nina: Heads-up — console prefetch for org/project metadata when you open the API keys page is generating a lot of backend requests and is skewing quota attribution to org-level instead of project-level. Spotted in prod around 03:10 UTC this morning.
raj: Ugh. Are we doing a full fetch for every visible key row? I thought we had lazy-loading for project info.
nina: Looks like the UI fires `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects?ids=[...]` for the whole page on mount. It then hits the auth service to expand service-account claims.
elaine: Can you paste the trace? is this causing rate limits?
nina: Trace snippet: ```
GET /api/keys?page=1
GET /v1/orgs/123/projects?ids=projA,projB,projC
POST /auth/expand
```
nina: The expand calls are the noisy ones — they include a quota-check per project which drives billing/telemetry events.
sam: Quick question: is this just telemetry noise or are real quotas getting charged to the wrong entity?
nina: Both. For short bursts it's mostly noise, but during the page load spike we saw ~500 requests attribute to the org bucket instead of the proxied project. Dashboard shows a jump.
raj: Might be because we use org-scoped token for the console backend and only attach project claim after expand — so quota middleware records before claim attach.
elaine: If we reorder so the expand happens earlier in the request path, can middleware re-attribute? Or is attribution locked at ingress?
sam: Attribution currently happens at ingress based on token principal header. Re-attr isn't supported safely (too many side effects).
raj: Options: 1) change UI to batch fewer expand requests and only for visible rows, 2) change console backend to call expand upfront and proxy a project-scoped header to middleware, or 3) suppress quota telemetry for expand flows (ugly).
elaine: I prefer 2) for correctness, but it's more invasive. 1) is quick and may reduce noise immediately.
nina: Proposed short-term: debounce the UI expand calls (200ms) and do per-visible-row fetch. Long-term: console backend should request project claims before hitting quota middleware (so middleware sees the correct effective identity).
sam: Agree. Also add a flag to mark expand as non-billable in telemetry so we can differentiate until we fix.
alerts-bot: incident-note: quota-attribution-anomaly detected (org: 123) — spike 03:03-03:20 UTC; alerted 03:25 UTC.
raj: I'll open a tiny PR for the UI debounce and file an infra ticket for middleware ordering. Nina — can you capture exact repro steps for the ticket?
nina: Yep, will paste steps and the reduced trace into the ticket.
elaine: Add an item to the dashboard: show "attribution source" (token vs expanded-claim) per spike. That will help ops triage.
sam: I'll own the telemetry flag change; will send a short RFC for marking expand flows non-billable for 30 days.
raj: Cool. Timeline: UI patch today, telemetry flag + RFC tomorrow, middleware design next week.
nina: Thanks all :thumbsup:
